"""Drive the real page in headless Chrome and check the Constellation tab end to end."""
import sys, time, json
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from cdp import Browser

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8766/"
results = []

def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    results.append((name, bool(ok)))
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + name + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))

with Browser() as b:
    js = b.eval
    b.open(URL)
    b.wait("document.getElementById('status').textContent === 'Ready.' || document.getElementById('status').textContent.startsWith('Error')", 150)
    check("page ready", js("document.getElementById('status').textContent") == "Ready.", js("document.getElementById('status').textContent"))
    b.wait("document.getElementById('n').textContent !== '–'", 30)
    n0 = int(js("document.getElementById('n').textContent"))
    check("GPS only at start: 24 satellites, some in view", js("app.cons.count()") == 24 and 7 <= n0 <= 12, f"count={js('app.cons.count()')}, in view={n0}")

    # --- Constellation tab ---
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-cs').click()")
    b.pump(0.5)
    check("Constellation tab is shown", js("!document.getElementById('tab-cs').hidden && document.getElementById('tab-mc').hidden && document.getElementById('tab-live').hidden"))
    check("four presets listed", js("document.querySelectorAll('#cs-presets .preset').length") == 4)
    check("GPS shows Remove, others Add", js("[...document.querySelectorAll('#cs-presets button')].map(x=>x.textContent).join(',')") == "Remove,Add,Add,Add",
          js("[...document.querySelectorAll('#cs-presets button')].map(x=>x.textContent).join(',')"))
    check("count text", js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent") == "(24 on of 24)", js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent"))
    b.screenshot("s4_tab.png")

    def click_preset(key): js(f"document.querySelector('#cs-presets button[data-key=\"{key}\"]').click()")
    def count(): return js("app.cons.count()")
    def in_view():
        b.pump(0.3); time.sleep(0.3); b.pump(0.3)
        return int(js("document.getElementById('n').textContent"))

    click_preset("galileo"); click_preset("beidou_meo"); click_preset("beidou_igso_geo")
    check("all four presets: 78 satellites", count() == 78, count())
    n_all = in_view()
    check("many more satellites in view with four systems", n_all > n0 + 8, f"{n0} -> {n_all}")
    check("count text updated", js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent") == "(78 on of 78)")
    check("GPS Remove, Galileo Remove ...", js("[...document.querySelectorAll('#cs-presets button')].map(x=>x.textContent).join(',')") == "Remove,Remove,Remove,Remove")
    # globe has 16 rings and 78 satellites: check through the scene via the app (rings counted by Python)
    info = json.loads(js("app.api.set_constellation(JSON.stringify(app.cons.activeElements()), JSON.stringify(app.cons.activeElements().map(()=>true)))"))
    check("16 distinct orbits", len(info["paths"]) == 16, len(info["paths"]))
    b.pump(0.5)
    check("no JS errors so far", not [e for e in b.errors if "favicon" not in e], b.errors[:3])
    b.screenshot("s4_all.png")

    # --- switching satellites off ---
    boxes = js("document.querySelectorAll('#cs-list input[data-act=\"sat-toggle\"]').length")
    check("satellite rows are rendered (collapsed groups still in DOM)", boxes == 78, boxes)
    js("document.querySelector('#cs-list input[data-act=\"grp-toggle\"][data-g=\"2\"]').click()")   # Galileo off
    n_off = in_view()
    check("Galileo switched off: count text and view change", js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent") == "(54 on of 78)" and n_off < n_all,
          f"{js('document.getElementById(\"cs-count\").textContent')}, in view {n_all}->{n_off}")
    js("document.querySelector('#cs-list input[data-act=\"grp-toggle\"][data-g=\"2\"]').click()")   # back on
    check("Galileo back on", in_view() == n_all)

    # --- add a custom satellite ---
    js("document.getElementById('cs-add').click()")
    b.pump(0.3)
    check("custom satellite added (X1)", count() == 79 and "Added X1" in js("document.getElementById('cs-msg').textContent"), js("document.getElementById('cs-msg').textContent"))
    # elliptical
    js("document.getElementById('cs-ell').click()"); b.pump(0.2)
    check("elliptical fields shown, label changed", js("!document.getElementById('cs-ell-fields').hidden") and "Perigee" in js("document.getElementById('cs-alt-label').textContent"))
    js("document.getElementById('cs-alt').value = '500'; document.getElementById('cs-alt').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.2)
    msg = js("document.getElementById('cs-msg').textContent")
    check("elliptical message shows e and period", "e = " in msg and "period" in msg, msg)
    js("document.getElementById('cs-add').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    check("elliptical satellite added", count() == 80)
    # invalid orbit
    js("document.getElementById('cs-alt').value = '100'; document.getElementById('cs-alt').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.2)
    check("low perigee gives an error and disables Add", js("document.getElementById('cs-msg').classList.contains('err') && document.getElementById('cs-add').disabled"),
          js("document.getElementById('cs-msg').textContent"))
    js("document.getElementById('cs-ell').click()"); b.pump(0.2)           # elliptical off
    # geostationary
    js("document.getElementById('cs-geo').click()"); b.pump(0.2)
    js("document.getElementById('cs-lon').value = '-75'; document.getElementById('cs-lon').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.2)
    check("geostationary form shown", js("!document.getElementById('cs-geo-fields').hidden && document.getElementById('cs-circ-fields').hidden"))
    js("document.getElementById('cs-add').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    check("geostationary satellite added", count() == 81)
    # check it hangs over -75 at two times
    for tt in (0, 40000):
        snap = json.loads(js(f"app.api.snapshot(0, -75, {tt})"))
        i = 80
        check(f"GEO satellite is overhead of (0, -75) at t={tt}", abs(snap['el'][i] - 90) < 1e-6 and abs(snap['sat_lon'][i] + 75) < 1e-6, f"el={snap['el'][i]:.4f}")
    # walker
    js("document.getElementById('cs-w-add').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    check("Walker 12/3/1 added", count() == 93, count())
    js("document.getElementById('cs-w-T').value = '13'; document.getElementById('cs-w-T').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.2)
    check("bad Walker gives an error", js("document.getElementById('cs-w-msg').classList.contains('err') && document.getElementById('cs-w-add').disabled"), js("document.getElementById('cs-w-msg').textContent"))
    in_view(); b.screenshot("s4_custom.png")

    # --- hover and click-to-toggle on the globe ---
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-live').click()"); b.pump(0.5)
    labels = js("app.cons.decorate({}).labels")
    # find a satellite on screen that is not hidden by the Earth by hovering each in turn
    target = None
    for i in range(len(labels)):
        p = js(f"app.globe.screenOf({i})")
        if not (40 < p["x"] < 1000 and 40 < p["y"] < 700): continue
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseMoved", x=p["x"], y=p["y"]); b.pump(0.4)
        if js("!document.getElementById('sat-tip').hidden") and labels[i] in js("document.getElementById('sat-tip').textContent"):
            target = (i, p); break
    check("hovering a satellite shows its tooltip", target is not None)
    if target:
        i, p = target
        tip = js("document.getElementById('sat-tip').textContent")
        check("tooltip names the satellite and its group, and offers the click", labels[i] in tip and "Click to switch off" in tip, tip[:90])
        on_before = js(f"app.cons.decorate({{}}) && document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent")
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mousePressed", x=p["x"], y=p["y"], button="left", clickCount=1)
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseReleased", x=p["x"], y=p["y"], button="left", clickCount=1)
        b.pump(0.5)
        after = js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent")
        check("clicking the satellite on the globe switches it off", after != on_before, f"{on_before} -> {after}")
        b.pump(0.3)
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseMoved", x=p["x"], y=p["y"]); b.pump(0.5)
        tip2 = js("document.getElementById('sat-tip').textContent") if js("!document.getElementById('sat-tip').hidden") else ""
        check("switched-off satellite says so", "switched off" in tip2 and "Click to switch on" in tip2, tip2[-80:])
        b.screenshot("s4_hover.png")

    # --- Monte Carlo uses the live constellation ---
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-mc').click()")
    b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-run').disabled === false", 150)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-n').value = '20000'; document.getElementById('mc-run').click()")
    b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent === 'Done.'", 120)
    cfg = js("document.getElementById('r-config').textContent")
    mean = js("document.getElementById('r-mean').textContent"); check_text = js("document.getElementById('r-check').textContent")
    nsat_on = int(js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent.match(/\\((\\d+) on/)[1]"))
    check("Monte Carlo reports the satellites it used and a 365-day window", cfg == f"{nsat_on} satellites / 365.0 days", cfg)
    print("   MC mean in view:", mean, "| analytic:", check_text)
    z = float(check_text.split("(")[1].split("σ")[0])
    check("Monte Carlo mean agrees with the analytic value (|z| < 4)", abs(z) < 4, f"z = {z}")
    b.screenshot("s4_mc.png")

    # --- reset ---
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-cs').click()"); js("document.getElementById('cs-reset').click()"); b.pump(0.5)
    check("reset returns to GPS only", count() == 24 and js("document.getElementById('cs-count').textContent") == "(24 on of 24)")
    # remove everything
    js("document.querySelector('#cs-presets button[data-key=\"gps\"]').click()"); b.pump(0.5)
    check("empty constellation: 0 satellites, page still alive", count() == 0 and js("document.getElementById('n').textContent") == "0", js("document.getElementById('n').textContent"))
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-mc').click()"); js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(0.5)
    check("Monte Carlo with no satellites explains why", "No satellites" in js("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent"), js("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent"))

    errs = [e for e in b.errors if "favicon" not in e]
    check("no JavaScript errors in the whole session", not errs, errs[:4])

passed = sum(ok for _, ok in results)
print(f"\n{passed}/{len(results)} checks passed")

import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from cdp import Browser

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8766/"

def check(name, ok, detail=""):

with Browser() as b:

    ang = js("JSON.parse(app.api.snapshot(40, -80, 21544.0225)).earth_angle_deg")

    js("document.getElementById('time').value = '500'; document.getElementById('time').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.6)
    b.screenshot("r_earth.png")
    placed = False
    for (x, y) in [(505, 380), (480, 400), (530, 360), (520, 420)]:         # points on the Earth's disc
        js("document.getElementById('lat').value = '0'; document.getElementById('lon').value = '0'")
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mousePressed", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1)
        b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseReleased", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1); b.pump(0.5)
        if js("document.getElementById('lat').value") != "0":
            placed = True; break
    lat, lon = float(js("document.getElementById('lat').value")), float(js("document.getElementById('lon').value"))

    snap_rx = js("JSON.parse(app.api.snapshot(%f, %f, app.cons ? 500*60 : 0)).receiver" % (lat, lon))
    check("receiver position is on the Earth's surface", abs((sum(v*v for v in snap_rx) ** 0.5) - 6378.137) < 1e-6)

    # --- Monte Carlo with visualization ---
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-mc').click()")
    b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-run').disabled === false", 150)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-viz').click()")
    check("rate controls enabled and legend shown", js("!document.getElementById('mc-rate-num').disabled && !document.getElementById('mc-legend').hidden"))
    js("document.getElementById('mc-n').value = '5000'; document.getElementById('mc-rate-num').value = '300'; document.getElementById('mc-rate-num').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()")
    b.pump(3.0)
    prog = js("document.getElementById('mc-progress').value")
    done_text = js("document.getElementById('r-done').textContent")
    check("run is progressing at about 300 trials/s", 0.05 < prog < 0.5, f"progress={prog:.3f}, done={done_text}")
    b.screenshot("r_viz.png")
    check("button says Cancel while running", js("document.getElementById('mc-run').textContent") == "Cancel")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(1.0)
    st = js("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent")
    check("Cancel stops the run and keeps the partial results", st.startswith("Cancelled") and js("document.getElementById('r-done').textContent") != "–", st)
    # the same seed run twice (not visualized) gives identical numbers
    js("document.getElementById('mc-viz').click()")
    outs = []
    for _ in range(2):
        js("document.getElementById('mc-n').value = '8000'; document.getElementById('mc-seed').value = '7'; document.getElementById('mc-run').click()")
        b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent === 'Done.'", 120)
        outs.append((js("document.getElementById('r-mean').textContent"), js("document.getElementById('r-avail').textContent"), js("document.getElementById('r-med').textContent")))
    check("same seed gives identical results", outs[0] == outs[1], outs[0])
    check("histograms were drawn", js("document.getElementById('hist-n').width") > 0 and js("document.getElementById('hist-dop').width") > 0)
    b.screenshot("r_mc.png")

    errs = [e for e in b.errors if "favicon" not in e]
    check("no JavaScript errors", not errs, errs[:4])

print(f"\n{sum(results)}/{len(results)} checks passed")

Step 4 is built and tested in a real browser. I'm giving you the results now.

## Testing in a real browser

I found Google Chrome on this machine, and I wrote a small helper that drives it headless. It loads the page, clicks and types, reads console errors and takes screenshots. This is the first time any of the web code has been run for real, not just reasoned about. That helper is in the scratchpad, not the repo.

- **Constellation tab:** 36 of 36 checks passed. Presets, switching satellites off, custom, elliptical, geostationary and Walker forms, hover and click on the globe, and Monte Carlo on the live constellation were all exercised.
- **Earlier features:** 13 of 14 passed. Play, the old tab-switch bug (time kept running while other tabs were open), visualized Monte Carlo, Cancel and same-seed repeatability all work. The one failure was a typo in my test (a quarter sidereal day is 21,541 s, not 21,544 s), not the app.
- **Earth picking:** clicking the globe's centre gives latitude 20.29° at three different times, with longitudes −56.31°, 178.35° and 53.01°. That matches my independent calculation exactly.
- **JavaScript errors:** none in any session.
- **Bug found and fixed:** the Kepler solver crashed when every satellite was switched off, so the page would have broken. A test now covers it.

## What you get

- **Tab:** a third tab, **Constellation**. Add or remove GPS, Galileo, BeiDou MEO and BeiDou IGSO+GEO. There is a per-satellite checkbox, a master box per constellation, delete for added satellites, and "Reset to GPS only".
- **Add forms:** the add-satellite form supports circular, elliptical and geostationary orbits, with live validation messages. A Walker T/P/F generator sits below it.
- **Click to toggle:** clicking a satellite on the globe switches it off or on.
- **Colours:** by constellation, and the orbit rings match.
- **Monte Carlo:** it now uses whichever satellites are on and shows how many it used.
- **Measured results:**
  - With all four systems, 9 satellites become **25 in view**.
  - The mixed-constellation Monte Carlo mean (35.64) agrees with the analytic value (35.69), at −1.9σ.
  - The geostationary satellite stays at elevation exactly 90° from its longitude.

## Things to know

- **Sky plot labels:** they hide when more than 14 satellites are in view, because they overlapped. The table lists them all.
- **Camera:** the default view doesn't fit the geostationary ring. Scroll to zoom out.
- **Monte Carlo window:** it is fixed at 365 days for now. I changed that assumption (A11) and added A16 and A17 to the README. The window control, the LCM toggle and the time snapping are step 5.
- **New page hook:** `window.app` is exposed for debugging in the console.
- **Python tests:** 162 pass.

## Not done

Nothing is committed. The colours were chosen by eye, and I couldn't run the palette validator without Node.

Decisions for you:
1. Commit step 4 now?
2. Add the browser test scripts to the repo, as `tools/browser_test/`? They would let you re-run these checks yourself, but they add about 300 lines for you to understand.
3. Go on to step 5?

def period_of(*keys):

    medians, means = [], []
    for window in (7 * 86400.0, 30 * 86400.0, 120 * 86400.0, 365 * 86400.0, lcm):

        medians.append(float(np.nanmedian(pdop)))

    assert max(medians) - min(medians) < 0.02
    assert max(means) - min(means) < 0.15

"""Entry points called from the web page (via Pyodide). Everything is returned
as a JSON string so the JavaScript side only has to draw it.

The page owns the list of satellites (names, colours, which are switched on) and sends the
numbers to Python with set_constellation(); snapshot() then works on that constellation."""

import json
import math

import numpy as np

from . import constellation, geometry, presets
from .dop import dop

DEFAULT_MASK_DEG = 0.0       # satellites below this elevation are not used (0 = geometric horizon)
MAX_SATELLITES = 300         # most satellites the page may hold at once
MAX_WALKER_SATELLITES = 120  # largest single Walker set

# The constellation snapshot() works on: an elements table and, for each satellite, whether it is
# switched on. Switched-off satellites are drawn as ghosts but do not count for visibility or DOP.
_state = {"elements": presets.gps(), "enabled": np.ones(24, dtype=bool)}


def _clean(x):
    """NaN is not valid JSON, so undefined DOP values become null."""
    return None if isinstance(x, float) and math.isnan(x) else x


# ---- the sky seen by one receiver ------------------------------------------------------------

def snapshot(lat_deg, lon_deg, t_seconds, mask_deg=DEFAULT_MASK_DEG):
    """State of the sky for a receiver at (lat, lon) at time t seconds."""
    elements, enabled = _state["elements"], _state["enabled"]
    sat = constellation.positions(elements, t_seconds)
    rx = geometry.receiver_position(lat_deg, lon_deg, t_seconds)   # inertial position: the Earth turns
    enu = geometry.enu_basis(lat_deg, lon_deg, t_seconds)
    az, el, unit = geometry.look_angles(rx, sat, enu)
    visible = (el >= mask_deg) & enabled                            # switched-off satellites never count

    values = dop(unit[visible], enu)
    sat_lat, sat_lon = geometry.lat_lon(sat, t_seconds)             # Earth-fixed point below each satellite
    return json.dumps({
        "t": t_seconds,
        "earth_angle_deg": float(geometry.earth_angle_deg(t_seconds)),
        "mask_deg": mask_deg,
        "receiver": rx.tolist(),
        # orbit information shown in the satellite hover tooltip
        "r_earth_km": geometry.R_EARTH,
        "elements": elements.tolist(),          # rows: a (km), e, inclination, RAAN, arg. of perigee, M0 (deg)
        "period_s": constellation.period(elements[:, constellation.A]).tolist(),
        "speed_kms": constellation.speed(elements, t_seconds).tolist(),
        "radius_km": constellation.radius(elements, t_seconds).tolist(),
        "perigee_alt_km": (constellation.perigee_radius(elements) - geometry.R_EARTH).tolist(),
        "apogee_alt_km": (constellation.apogee_radius(elements) - geometry.R_EARTH).tolist(),
        "nu_deg": constellation.true_anomaly_deg(elements, t_seconds).tolist(),
        "u_deg": constellation.argument_of_latitude(elements, t_seconds).tolist(),
        "sat_lat": sat_lat.tolist(),
        "sat_lon": sat_lon.tolist(),
        "sat_positions": sat.tolist(),
        "az": az.tolist(),
        "el": el.tolist(),
        "enabled": enabled.tolist(),
        "visible": visible.tolist(),
        "n_visible": int(visible.sum()),
        "dop": {k: _clean(v) for k, v in values.items()},
    })


# ---- the constellation --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def orbit_paths(elements, n=181):
    """Points around each distinct orbit (for drawing it) and, for every satellite, which orbit
    it is on. Satellites that differ only in their phase share an orbit (one ring)."""
    index, paths, ring_of = {}, [], []
    for row in elements:
        key = tuple(np.round(row[:constellation.M0], 9))          # same orbit if all but the phase match
        if key not in index:
            index[key] = len(paths)
            paths.append(constellation.orbit_path(row, n).tolist())
        ring_of.append(index[key])
    return paths, ring_of


def set_constellation(elements_json, enabled_json):
    """Replace the constellation. Returns the orbit rings to draw: {"paths", "ring_of"}."""
    elements = np.array(json.loads(elements_json), dtype=float).reshape(-1, 6)
    enabled = np.array(json.loads(enabled_json), dtype=bool).reshape(-1)
    if len(elements) != len(enabled):
        raise ValueError("elements and enabled flags must have the same length")
    if len(elements) > MAX_SATELLITES:
        raise ValueError(f"at most {MAX_SATELLITES} satellites are allowed")
    _state["elements"], _state["enabled"] = elements, enabled
    paths, ring_of = orbit_paths(elements)
    return json.dumps({"paths": paths, "ring_of": ring_of})


def preset_info():
    """The ready-made constellations: key, label, label prefix, system, number of satellites."""
    return json.dumps([{"key": key, "label": p["label"], "short": p["short"], "system": p["system"],
                        "count": len(p["build"]())} for key, p in presets.PRESETS.items()])


def preset_elements(key):
    p = presets.PRESETS[key]
    return json.dumps({"elements": p["build"]().tolist(), "names": p["names"]()})


# ---- building satellites from the forms ---------------------------------------------------------------

def _number(params, key, label):
    value = params.get(key)
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a number")
    return float(value)


def _orbit_info(row):
    a, ecc = row[constellation.A], row[constellation.ECC]
    return {"a_km": a, "ecc": ecc, "period_s": float(constellation.period(a)),
            "perigee_alt_km": a * (1.0 - ecc) - geometry.R_EARTH,
            "apogee_alt_km": a * (1.0 + ecc) - geometry.R_EARTH}


def orbit_from_form(params_json):
    """One satellite from the 'add a satellite' form. Returns {"ok": true, "elements": [6 numbers],
    "info": {...}} or {"ok": false, "error": "message"}.

    params: geo (geostationary: only lon is used), lon, alt (altitude, km; the perigee altitude if
    elliptical), inc, raan, phase (mean anomaly at t = 0), elliptical, apogee (altitude, km), argp."""
    try:
        p = json.loads(params_json)
        if p.get("geo"):
            row = constellation.geostationary(_number(p, "lon", "longitude"))
        else:
            hp = _number(p, "alt", "altitude")
            inc = _number(p, "inc", "inclination")
            raan = _number(p, "raan", "RAAN")
            phase = _number(p, "phase", "starting phase")
            if p.get("elliptical"):
                ha = _number(p, "apogee", "apogee altitude")
                argp = _number(p, "argp", "argument of perigee")
                if ha < hp:
                    raise ValueError("apogee altitude must be at least the perigee altitude")
                a = geometry.R_EARTH + (hp + ha) / 2.0
                ecc = (ha - hp) / (ha + hp + 2.0 * geometry.R_EARTH)
            else:
                a, ecc, argp = geometry.R_EARTH + hp, 0.0, 0.0
            constellation.validate_orbit(a, ecc, inc)
            row = constellation.make_elements(a, ecc, inc, raan, argp, phase)
        return json.dumps({"ok": True, "elements": row[0].tolist(), "info": _orbit_info(row[0])})
    except ValueError as err:
        return json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": str(err)})


def walker_from_form(params_json):
    """A Walker T/P/F constellation. Returns {"ok": true, "elements": [...], "names": [...]} or
    {"ok": false, "error": "message"}. params: T, P, F, alt (altitude, km), inc."""
    try:
        p = json.loads(params_json)
        T, P, F = (_number(p, k, k) for k in ("T", "P", "F"))
        if not (T.is_integer() and P.is_integer() and F.is_integer()):
            raise ValueError("T, P and F must be whole numbers")
        T, P, F = int(T), int(P), int(F)
        alt, inc = _number(p, "alt", "altitude"), _number(p, "inc", "inclination")
        if not 1 <= P <= 26:
            raise ValueError("P (planes) must be between 1 and 26")
        if T < P or T % P != 0:
            raise ValueError("T (satellites) must be a multiple of P (planes)")
        if T > MAX_WALKER_SATELLITES:
            raise ValueError(f"T may be at most {MAX_WALKER_SATELLITES}")
        if not 0 <= F <= P - 1:
            raise ValueError(f"F must be between 0 and P - 1 = {P - 1}")
        a = geometry.R_EARTH + alt
        constellation.validate_orbit(a, 0.0, inc)
        return json.dumps({"ok": True, "elements": constellation.walker(T, P, F, a, inc).tolist(),
                           "names": constellation.names(T, P)})
    except ValueError as err:
        return json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": str(err)})

"""Monte-Carlo estimate of coverage and DOP.

Each trial picks a random receiver location (uniform over the sphere's surface)
and a random time, then records how many satellites are above the elevation
mask and the DOP values. A trial is "good" if it has at least 4 satellites and
PDOP <= pdop_max.

All random numbers for a run are drawn once, up front, from one seeded
generator. So the results depend only on (seed, n), never on how the run is
split into chunks.
"""

import json
import math

import numpy as np

from . import constellation, geometry, presets
from .dop import KEYS, dop_batch

MAX_TRIALS = 1_000_000
SUB_CHUNK = 20_000      # trials per vectorized batch (bounds memory)
HIST_BINS = 40
DEFAULT_WINDOW_S = 365 * 86400.0    # random times are drawn from [0, window): one year by default


# ---- sampling ------------------------------------------------------------------

def sample_locations(rng, n):
    """n random (lat, lon) in degrees, uniform by AREA on the sphere.

    The surface area between latitudes is proportional to the change in
    sin(lat), so sin(lat) is drawn uniformly on [-1, 1] (drawing lat itself
    uniformly would over-sample the poles).
    """
    lat = np.degrees(np.arcsin(rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, n)))
    lon = rng.uniform(-180.0, 180.0, n)
    return lat, lon


def sample_times(rng, n, window):
    """n random times uniform on [0, window) seconds."""
    return rng.uniform(0.0, window, n)


# ---- analytic coverage (used as a check) -----------------------------------------

sub("  function addCustomSatellite(elements) {\n    room(1);", "  function addCustomSatellite(elements) {\n    if (locked) return \"\";\n    room(1);")
sub("  function addWalker(T, P, F, data) {\n    room(data.elements.length);", "  function addWalker(T, P, F, data) {\n    if (locked) return;\n    room(data.elements.length);")

"""Step 5 in the real page: the time window, the common-repeat-period toggle, and time snapping/locking."""

from cdp import Browser

results = []
def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    results.append(bool(ok)); print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + name + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))

    for _ in range(50):
        try: b.open("http://127.0.0.1:8766/"); break
        except Exception: time.sleep(0.2)
    b.wait("document.getElementById('status').textContent === 'Ready.'", 150)
    b.wait("document.getElementById('n').textContent !== '–'", 30)
    def tab(name): js(f"document.getElementById('tab-btn-{name}').click()"); b.pump(0.4)
    def val(id): return js(f"document.getElementById('{id}').value")
    def text(id): return js(f"document.getElementById('{id}').textContent")
    def setv(id, v, ev="input"): js(f"document.getElementById('{id}').value = '{v}'; document.getElementById('{id}').dispatchEvent(new Event('{ev}', {{bubbles: true}}))"); b.pump(0.2)

    tab("mc"); b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-run').disabled === false", 150)
    check("window box defaults to 365 days, LCM off", val("mc-window") == "365" and not js("document.getElementById('mc-lcm').checked"))
    info = text("mc-window-info")
    check("GPS alone: common repeat period is one orbit (0.50 days)", "Common repeat period 0.50 days" in info and "mismatch 0.0" in info, info)

    # all four systems
    tab("cs")
    for key in ("galileo", "beidou_meo", "beidou_igso_geo"): js(f"document.querySelector('#cs-presets button[data-key=\"{key}\"]').click()")
    tab("mc")
    info = text("mc-window-info")
    check("four systems: repeat period 69.81 days, window is 5.23 cycles", "69.81 days" in info and "5.23 repeat cycles" in info, info)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-lcm').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    check("LCM toggle: window box shows the repeat period and is locked", js("document.getElementById('mc-window').disabled") and abs(float(val("mc-window")) - 69.8115) < 0.001, val("mc-window"))
    check("info says the window is 1.00 cycles", "1.00 repeat cycles" in text("mc-window-info"), text("mc-window-info"))
    # constellation change updates the window while LCM is on
    tab("cs"); js("document.querySelector('#cs-presets button[data-key=\"beidou_igso_geo\"]').click()"); tab("mc")
    w3 = float(val("mc-window"))
    check("removing BeiDou IGSO+GEO changes the LCM window", abs(w3 - 69.8115) > 0.5, f"{w3}")
    tab("cs"); js("document.querySelector('#cs-presets button[data-key=\"beidou_igso_geo\"]').click()"); tab("mc")
    check("adding it back restores 69.81 days", abs(float(val("mc-window")) - 69.8115) < 0.001)

    # a run with the LCM window
    setv("mc-n", "3000", "input")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent === 'Done.'", 120)
    check("run used the LCM window", text("r-config") == "78 satellites / 69.8 days", text("r-config"))
    # a typed window
    js("document.getElementById('mc-lcm').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    check("LCM off: window box is editable again", not js("document.getElementById('mc-window').disabled"))
    setv("mc-window", "30")
    check("typed 30 days: info shows the ratio", "0.43 repeat cycles" in text("mc-window-info"), text("mc-window-info"))
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent === 'Done.'", 120)
    check("run used the typed 30-day window", text("r-config") == "78 satellites / 30.0 days", text("r-config"))
    setv("mc-window", "abc"); 
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-status').textContent === 'Done.'", 120)
    check("invalid window falls back to 365 days", text("r-config") == "78 satellites / 365.0 days", text("r-config"))

    # no common period: a constellation of 8 unrelated orbits
    tab("cs"); js("document.getElementById('cs-reset').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    for alt in (1700, 5000, 8500, 12500, 17000, 22500, 28000, 33500):
        setv("cs-alt", alt); js("document.getElementById('cs-add').click()"); b.pump(0.1)
    tab("mc"); js("document.getElementById('mc-lcm').click()"); b.pump(0.3)
    info = text("mc-window-info")
    check("no common period: says so and keeps the typed window", "No common repeat period" in info and "Using the typed window" in info and not js("document.getElementById('mc-window').disabled"), info)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-lcm').click()")
    tab("cs"); js("document.getElementById('cs-reset').click()"); b.pump(0.3)

    # ---- time snapping and locking (visualized run) ----
    tab("mc")
    setv("mc-window", "365")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-viz').click()")
    setv("mc-rate-num", "100"); setv("mc-n", "6000")
    t0 = js("document.getElementById('tlabel').textContent")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()")
    b.pump(2.6)
    tab("live")
    locked = js("['lat','lon','time','play','speed'].every(id => document.getElementById(id).disabled)")
    check("Live controls are locked during the run", locked)
    note = text("live-lock-note")
    check("lock note shows the featured trial", not js("document.getElementById('live-lock-note').hidden") and note.startswith("Monte Carlo trial"), note)
    m = re.search(r"trial ([\d,]+): latitude (-?[\d.]+)°, longitude (-?[\d.]+)°, day (\d+)", note)
    label = text("tlabel")
    check("timeline shows the trial's day", m and label.startswith(f"Day {m.group(4)} "), f"{label} | {note}")
    check("time snapped far from the start (a random time within the year)", label != t0 and int(m.group(4)) >= 0, label)
    first = label
    b.pump(2.2)
    label2 = text("tlabel")
    check("time keeps snapping to new trials", label2 != first, f"{first} -> {label2}")
    idx = [int(re.search(r"trial ([\d,]+)", text("live-lock-note")).group(1).replace(",", ""))]
    check("featured trials are every 100th trial", idx[0] % 100 == 0, idx)
    check("sky plot and readout show the featured trial", text("n") != "–" and js("document.getElementById('sky').width") > 0, f"{text('n')} in view, GDOP {text('gdop')}")
    b.screenshot("s5_live_locked.png")
    tab("cs")
    check("Constellation tab is locked during the run", js("document.getElementById('cs-add').disabled && !document.getElementById('cs-lock-note').hidden && document.querySelector('#cs-presets button').disabled"))
    js("document.querySelector('#cs-list input[data-act=\"sat-toggle\"]')?.click()")
    check("clicking a satellite while locked does nothing", text("cs-count") == "(78 on of 78)", text("cs-count"))
    tab("mc"); check("window controls locked during the run", js("document.getElementById('mc-window').disabled && document.getElementById('mc-lcm').disabled"))
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(1.0)           # Cancel
    check("run cancelled", text("mc-status").startswith("Cancelled"), text("mc-status"))
    tab("live")
    check("Live controls unlocked after the run", js("['lat','lon','time','play','speed'].every(id => !document.getElementById(id).disabled) && document.getElementById('live-lock-note').hidden"))
    tab("cs")
    check("Constellation controls unlocked after the run", js("!document.querySelector('#cs-presets button').disabled && !document.getElementById('cs-add').disabled && document.getElementById('cs-lock-note').hidden"))
    js("document.getElementById('cs-add').click()"); b.pump(0.2)
    check("and editing works again", text("cs-count") == "(79 on of 79)", text("cs-count"))

    # ---- not visualized: controls lock but the time stays frozen ----
    tab("live"); setv("time", "300"); t_before = text("tlabel")
    tab("mc"); js("document.getElementById('mc-viz').click()")
    setv("mc-n", "1000000"); js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(1.5)
    tab("live")
    check("without Visualize the controls lock too", js("['lat','lon','time','play'].every(id => document.getElementById(id).disabled)"))
    check("without Visualize the time stays frozen", text("tlabel") == t_before, f"{t_before} -> {text('tlabel')}")
    tab("mc"); js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(1.0)

    errs = [e for e in b.errors if "favicon" not in e]
    check("no JavaScript errors", not errs, errs[:4])
print(f"\n{sum(results)}/{len(results)} checks passed")
EOF

Step 5 is done, and with it all of Stage 3. Everything was tested in headless Chrome on the real page, all 167 Python tests pass, and nothing is committed yet.

## What's new

- **Time window:** a "Window (days)" box in the Monte Carlo tab, defaulting to 365. Invalid input falls back to 365.
- **Common repeat period (LCM) checkbox:** it sets the window to the time after which all the switched-on satellites line up again.
  - The box locks and updates itself when you add or switch off satellites.
  - The tab shows the period, the worst phase mismatch, and how many repeat cycles your window covers. GPS alone is 0.50 days. All four systems give 69.81 days with a 5.9° mismatch, so a 365-day window covers 5.23 cycles.
  - If no common period exists within 10 years, it says so and keeps your typed window.
- **Time snapping:**
  - During a visualized run, every n-th trial (n = trials/s, so about one per second) becomes the featured trial. The globe, the Earth's rotation, the timeline ("Day 256 08:05:43"), the receiver marker, the sky plot and the readout all jump to that trial.
  - A note names the trial and where it is.
  - Without Visualize, time stays frozen.
- **Locking during a run:** the time, receiver and Play controls and the whole Constellation tab are locked, so the live view can't drift away from the satellites the run is using. Everything unlocks after Done or Cancel.

## How it was checked

- **Window doesn't change the answer:** for all four systems, the median PDOP is 0.807 for windows of 7, 30, 120 and 365 days and for the LCM. That backs up the 365-day default.
- **Python tests:** these check the common period function: GPS alone, the four systems at 70 sidereal days, no satellites, and no repeat. They also check that each trial's time falls inside the window.
- **Browser:** the step 5 suite passed 30 of 30. The step 4 suite (36/36) and the earlier-features suite (14/14) still pass, with no JavaScript errors.
- **My own test mistakes:** five checks failed on the first run, all because of wrong numbers in my test. For example, 70 sidereal days is 69.8089 days, not 69.8115, and I'd forgotten my script reset the satellites to GPS only. I corrected the test, not the code.

## README

A11 now describes the editable window and the checkbox, along with the window-independence result. A17 describes how the checkbox works. I updated the change-log entry to match.

Should I commit step 5? Stage 4, the valley that blocks part of the sky, is next whenever you're ready.

content.text:
Step 5 is committed as `bd3855b`. `journal/` had no changes to add.

The new time controls involve a few choices only you can make. One of them touches a physics assumption.

questions.question: What should the calendar control set? Right now t = 0 is an arbitrary moment (no real date), and the Earth's angle at t = 0 is arbitrary too (README assumption A2).

options.label: Day number picker (Recommended)
options.description: A 'Day' number box (0, 1, 2, ...) next to the time of day, with -/+ buttons. Keeps the arbitrary epoch, so no assumption changes. Simple and honest: there is no real date in the model.

"""Receiver geometry: where a receiver is, and where a satellite appears in its sky.

Earth is a perfect sphere of radius R_EARTH (km) that rotates at the sidereal rate.

Frames: the satellites live in a fixed (inertial) frame with +z through the north
pole. The Earth turns about +z, so a receiver at fixed (lat, lon) on the ground moves
through that frame. At t = 0 the Earth-fixed longitude 0 points along inertial +x.
Latitude/longitude arguments below are always Earth-fixed (what a map shows); the
time argument t (seconds) says how far the Earth has turned.

Every function works on a single receiver or on a whole array of receivers
(Monte Carlo trials): extra leading array dimensions are carried through.
"""

import numpy as np

R_EARTH = 6378.137          # km (WGS-84 equatorial radius, used as the sphere radius)
T_SIDEREAL = 86164.0905     # s, one rotation of the Earth relative to the stars
OMEGA_EARTH = 2.0 * np.pi / T_SIDEREAL   # rad/s


def earth_angle_deg(t):
    """Angle (degrees) the Earth has turned t seconds after t = 0."""
    return np.degrees(OMEGA_EARTH * np.asarray(t, dtype=float))


def receiver_position(lat_deg, lon_deg, t=0.0):
    """Receiver position (km) in the inertial frame at time t: shape (..., 3)."""
    lat, lon = np.broadcast_arrays(np.radians(lat_deg), np.radians(np.asarray(lon_deg) + earth_angle_deg(t)))
    return R_EARTH * np.stack([np.cos(lat) * np.cos(lon),
                               np.cos(lat) * np.sin(lon),
                               np.sin(lat)], axis=-1)

    """Julian Date of a UTC calendar date (Gregorian calendar), Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 7."""

    """Greenwich Mean Sidereal Time (degrees, 0-360) at Julian Date jd (UT), Meeus eq. 12.4."""
    T = (jd - 2451545.0) / 36525.0
    theta = 280.46061837 + 360.98564736629 * (jd - 2451545.0) + 0.000387933 * T**2 - T**3 / 38710000.0
    return theta % 360.0


EPOCH_UTC = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"                 # t = 0
EPOCH_JD = julian_date(2026, 1, 1)                 # 2461041.5
EARTH_ANGLE_AT_EPOCH = gmst_deg(EPOCH_JD)          # degrees, about 100.3

    """Angle (degrees) from inertial +x to longitude 0 at t seconds after the epoch: the GMST,
    which grows at the sidereal rate (one turn per 86,164.0905 s)."""
    return EARTH_ANGLE_AT_EPOCH + np.degrees(OMEGA_EARTH * np.asarray(t, dtype=float))

"""Receiver geometry: where a receiver is, and where a satellite appears in its sky.

Earth is a perfect sphere of radius R_EARTH (km) that rotates at the sidereal rate.

Frames: the satellites live in a fixed (inertial) frame with +z through the north
pole. The Earth turns about +z, so a receiver at fixed (lat, lon) on the ground moves
through that frame. At t = 0 the Earth-fixed longitude 0 points along inertial +x.
Latitude/longitude arguments below are always Earth-fixed (what a map shows); the
time argument t (seconds) says how far the Earth has turned.

Every function works on a single receiver or on a whole array of receivers
(Monte Carlo trials): extra leading array dimensions are carried through.
"""

import numpy as np

R_EARTH = 6378.137          # km (WGS-84 equatorial radius, used as the sphere radius)
T_SIDEREAL = 86164.0905     # s, one rotation of the Earth relative to the stars
OMEGA_EARTH = 2.0 * np.pi / T_SIDEREAL   # rad/s


def earth_angle_deg(t):
    """Angle (degrees) the Earth has turned t seconds after t = 0."""
    return np.degrees(OMEGA_EARTH * np.asarray(t, dtype=float))


def receiver_position(lat_deg, lon_deg, t=0.0):
    """Receiver position (km) in the inertial frame at time t: shape (..., 3)."""
    lat, lon = np.broadcast_arrays(np.radians(lat_deg), np.radians(np.asarray(lon_deg) + earth_angle_deg(t)))
    return R_EARTH * np.stack([np.cos(lat) * np.cos(lon),
                               np.cos(lat) * np.sin(lon),
                               np.sin(lat)], axis=-1)


def enu_basis(lat_deg, lon_deg, t=0.0):
    """Local East, North, Up unit vectors (inertial frame, at time t) as the rows of a
    3x3 matrix: shape (..., 3, 3).

    Multiplying a vector by this matrix gives its (east, north, up) components.
    """
    lat, lon = np.broadcast_arrays(np.radians(lat_deg), np.radians(np.asarray(lon_deg) + earth_angle_deg(t)))
    east = np.stack([-np.sin(lon), np.cos(lon), np.zeros_like(lon)], axis=-1)
    north = np.stack([-np.sin(lat) * np.cos(lon), -np.sin(lat) * np.sin(lon), np.cos(lat)], axis=-1)
    up = np.stack([np.cos(lat) * np.cos(lon), np.cos(lat) * np.sin(lon), np.sin(lat)], axis=-1)
    return np.stack([east, north, up], axis=-2)


def lat_lon(positions, t=0.0):
    """Earth-fixed latitude and longitude (degrees, longitude in [-180, 180)) of the point
    straight below each inertial position at time t (the inverse of receiver_position,
    ignoring height). Works on shape (..., 3)."""
    p = np.asarray(positions, dtype=float)
    r = np.linalg.norm(p, axis=-1)
    lon = np.degrees(np.arctan2(p[..., 1], p[..., 0])) - earth_angle_deg(t)
    return np.degrees(np.arcsin(p[..., 2] / r)), (lon + 180.0) % 360.0 - 180.0


def look_angles(rx, sat_positions, enu):
    """Azimuth, elevation and line-of-sight unit vectors from receiver(s) to satellites.

    Shapes for a single receiver: rx (3,), sat_positions (N, 3), enu (3, 3).
    For M receivers: rx (M, 3), sat_positions (M, N, 3), enu (M, 3, 3).

    Returns (az_deg, el_deg, unit_los):
      az_deg  : degrees clockwise from north, in [0, 360)       shape (..., N)
      el_deg  : degrees above the local horizontal plane        shape (..., N)
      unit_los: unit vectors from the receiver toward each satellite
                (same fixed frame as the positions)              shape (..., N, 3)
    """
    d = sat_positions - rx[..., None, :]

Frames: the satellites live in a fixed (inertial) frame with +z through the north
pole and +x toward the vernal equinox (the direction astronomers measure sidereal
time from). The Earth turns about +z, so a receiver at fixed (lat, lon) on the
ground moves through that frame. Latitude/longitude arguments below are always
Earth-fixed (what a map shows).

Time: t is seconds after the epoch, 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. The angle between
longitude 0 (Greenwich) and +x is the Greenwich Mean Sidereal Time (GMST), so a
calendar date and time fixes where the Earth is turned. (Precession, nutation,
polar motion and the small UTC/UT1 difference are ignored.)

Every function works on a single receiver or on a whole array of receivers
(Monte Carlo trials): extra leading array dimensions are carried through.
"""

import numpy as np

R_EARTH = 6378.137          # km (WGS-84 equatorial radius, used as the sphere radius)
T_SIDEREAL = 86164.0905     # s, one rotation of the Earth relative to the stars
OMEGA_EARTH = 2.0 * np.pi / T_SIDEREAL   # rad/s


def julian_date(year, month, day, hour=0.0):
    """Julian Date of a UTC calendar date (Gregorian calendar), Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 7."""
    if month <= 2:
        year, month = year - 1, month + 12
    a = year // 100
    b = 2 - a + a // 4
    return int(365.25 * (year + 4716)) + int(30.6001 * (month + 1)) + day + hour / 24.0 + b - 1524.5


def gmst_deg(jd):
    """Greenwich Mean Sidereal Time (degrees, 0-360) at Julian Date jd (UT), Meeus eq. 12.4."""
    T = (jd - 2451545.0) / 36525.0
    theta = 280.46061837 + 360.98564736629 * (jd - 2451545.0) + 0.000387933 * T**2 - T**3 / 38710000.0
    return theta % 360.0


EPOCH_UTC = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"                 # t = 0
EPOCH_JD = julian_date(2026, 1, 1)                 # 2461041.5
EARTH_ANGLE_AT_EPOCH = gmst_deg(EPOCH_JD)          # degrees, about 100.3


def earth_angle_deg(t):
    """Angle (degrees) from inertial +x to longitude 0 at t seconds after the epoch: the GMST,
    which grows at the sidereal rate (one turn per 86,164.0905 s)."""
    return EARTH_ANGLE_AT_EPOCH + np.degrees(OMEGA_EARTH * np.asarray(t, dtype=float))

"""Checks receiver geometry: positions, local frame, elevation and azimuth."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from sim import constellation as c
from sim import geometry as g


def look(lat, lon, sat):
    rx = g.receiver_position(lat, lon)
    return g.look_angles(rx, np.array([sat], dtype=float), g.enu_basis(lat, lon))


def test_receiver_positions():
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 0), [g.R_EARTH, 0, 0])
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 90), [0, g.R_EARTH, 0], atol=1e-9)
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(90, 0), [0, 0, g.R_EARTH], atol=1e-9)


def test_enu_at_lat0_lon0():
    east, north, up = g.enu_basis(0, 0)
    assert np.allclose(east, [0, 1, 0])
    assert np.allclose(north, [0, 0, 1])
    assert np.allclose(up, [1, 0, 0])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("lat,lon", [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (89.0, 10.0)])
def test_enu_is_orthonormal_and_right_handed(lat, lon):
    B = g.enu_basis(lat, lon)
    assert np.allclose(B @ B.T, np.eye(3))
    assert np.allclose(np.cross(B[0], B[1]), B[2])        # east x north = up


@pytest.mark.parametrize("lat,lon", [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (89.0, 10.0), (-10, -179)])
def test_lat_lon_inverts_receiver_position(lat, lon):
    la, lo = g.lat_lon(g.receiver_position(lat, lon))
    assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)
    la, lo = g.lat_lon(3.0 * g.receiver_position(lat, lon))        # height does not matter
    assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)


def test_satellite_ground_latitude_never_exceeds_inclination():
    """With 55 deg inclination the sub-satellite latitude stays within +-55 deg and reaches it."""
    elements = c.walker(24, 6, 1)
    lats = np.array([g.lat_lon(c.positions(elements, t))[0] for t in np.linspace(0, c.period(c.A_GPS), 400)])
    assert np.abs(lats).max() <= 55.0 + 1e-9
    assert np.abs(lats).max() > 54.9


# ---- rotating Earth ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_earth_turns_once_per_sidereal_day():
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(0.0), 0.0)
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(g.T_SIDEREAL), 360.0)
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(g.T_SIDEREAL / 4), 90.0)
    assert abs(g.T_SIDEREAL / 3600 - 23.9345) < 1e-3                   # 23 h 56 min 4 s


def test_receiver_moves_with_the_earth():
    quarter = g.T_SIDEREAL / 4
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 0, quarter), [0, g.R_EARTH, 0], atol=1e-6)    # lon 0 -> +y
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(90, 0, quarter), [0, 0, g.R_EARTH], atol=1e-6)   # pole stays put
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(40, -80, g.T_SIDEREAL), g.receiver_position(40, -80), atol=1e-6)


def test_local_frame_turns_with_the_earth():
    east, north, up = g.enu_basis(0, 0, g.T_SIDEREAL / 4)
    assert np.allclose(east, [-1, 0, 0], atol=1e-12)    # east, up, north all carried round by 90 degrees
    assert np.allclose(up, [0, 1, 0], atol=1e-12)
    assert np.allclose(north, [0, 0, 1], atol=1e-12)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("t", [0.0, 1000.0, 30000.0, 86164.0905, 400000.0])
def test_lat_lon_inverts_receiver_position_at_any_time(t):
    for lat, lon in [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (-10, -179)]:
        la, lo = g.lat_lon(g.receiver_position(lat, lon, t), t)
        assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)


def test_geostationary_satellite_hangs_over_one_spot():
    a_geo = c.geostationary_radius()
    assert abs(a_geo - 42164.17) < 0.05
    assert np.isclose(c.period(a_geo), g.T_SIDEREAL)                    # period = one sidereal day
    lon_sat = 77.5
    one = c.geostationary(lon_sat)                                      # equatorial circle, phase = longitude at t=0
    for t in np.linspace(0, 3 * g.T_SIDEREAL, 25):
        lat, lon = g.lat_lon(c.positions(one, t), t)
        assert np.isclose(lat[0], 0.0, atol=1e-9) and np.isclose(lon[0], lon_sat, atol=1e-9)
        # seen from the equator right below it, it stays at the zenith all the time

"""Checks receiver geometry: positions, local frame, elevation and azimuth."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from sim import constellation as c
from sim import geometry as g

# The geometry tests below are easiest to read when longitude 0 points along inertial +x, i.e. when
# the Earth's angle (GMST) is 0. That happens T0 seconds after the epoch (the Earth is turned about
# 100 degrees at the epoch itself).
T0 = ((360.0 - g.EARTH_ANGLE_AT_EPOCH) % 360.0) / np.degrees(g.OMEGA_EARTH)


def look(lat, lon, sat):
    rx = g.receiver_position(lat, lon, T0)
    return g.look_angles(rx, np.array([sat], dtype=float), g.enu_basis(lat, lon, T0))


def test_earth_angle_is_zero_at_T0():
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(T0) % 360.0, 0.0, atol=1e-9)


def test_receiver_positions():
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 0, T0), [g.R_EARTH, 0, 0])
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 90, T0), [0, g.R_EARTH, 0], atol=1e-6)
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(90, 0, T0), [0, 0, g.R_EARTH], atol=1e-6)


def test_enu_at_lat0_lon0():
    east, north, up = g.enu_basis(0, 0, T0)
    assert np.allclose(east, [0, 1, 0])
    assert np.allclose(north, [0, 0, 1])
    assert np.allclose(up, [1, 0, 0])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("lat,lon", [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (89.0, 10.0)])
def test_enu_is_orthonormal_and_right_handed(lat, lon):
    B = g.enu_basis(lat, lon)
    assert np.allclose(B @ B.T, np.eye(3))
    assert np.allclose(np.cross(B[0], B[1]), B[2])        # east x north = up


@pytest.mark.parametrize("lat,lon", [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (89.0, 10.0), (-10, -179)])
def test_lat_lon_inverts_receiver_position(lat, lon):
    la, lo = g.lat_lon(g.receiver_position(lat, lon))
    assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)
    la, lo = g.lat_lon(3.0 * g.receiver_position(lat, lon))        # height does not matter
    assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)


def test_satellite_ground_latitude_never_exceeds_inclination():
    """With 55 deg inclination the sub-satellite latitude stays within +-55 deg and reaches it."""
    elements = c.walker(24, 6, 1)
    lats = np.array([g.lat_lon(c.positions(elements, t))[0] for t in np.linspace(0, c.period(c.A_GPS), 400)])
    assert np.abs(lats).max() <= 55.0 + 1e-9
    assert np.abs(lats).max() > 54.9


# ---- rotating Earth ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_earth_turns_once_per_sidereal_day():
    a0 = g.earth_angle_deg(0.0)
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(g.T_SIDEREAL) - a0, 360.0)
    assert np.isclose(g.earth_angle_deg(g.T_SIDEREAL / 4) - a0, 90.0)
    assert abs(g.T_SIDEREAL / 3600 - 23.9345) < 1e-3                   # 23 h 56 min 4 s


def test_receiver_moves_with_the_earth():
    quarter = g.T_SIDEREAL / 4
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(0, 0, T0 + quarter), [0, g.R_EARTH, 0], atol=1e-6)    # lon 0 -> +y
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(90, 0, quarter), [0, 0, g.R_EARTH], atol=1e-6)        # pole stays put
    assert np.allclose(g.receiver_position(40, -80, g.T_SIDEREAL), g.receiver_position(40, -80), atol=1e-6)


# ---- the calendar: Julian Date and Greenwich sidereal time ----------------------------------------

def test_julian_date_published_values():
    assert g.julian_date(2000, 1, 1, 12.0) == 2451545.0                 # the J2000.0 epoch
    assert g.julian_date(1987, 4, 10) == 2446895.5                      # Meeus, example 12.a
    assert g.julian_date(1957, 10, 4, 19.0 + 26.0 / 60 + 24.0 / 3600) - 2436116.31 < 1e-3   # Meeus example 7.a (Sputnik)
    assert g.EPOCH_JD == 2461041.5                                       # 2026-01-01 0h UT


def test_gmst_matches_the_published_worked_examples():
    """Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, example 12.a: 1987 April 10, 0h UT, GMST = 13h 10m 46.3668s
    = 197.693195 deg. Example 12.b: same day 19h 21m 00s UT, GMST = 128.737873 deg."""
    assert abs(g.gmst_deg(2446895.5) - 197.693195) < 1e-5
    assert abs(g.gmst_deg(g.julian_date(1987, 4, 10, 19 + 21 / 60)) - 128.737873) < 1e-5


def test_earth_angle_is_the_gmst_of_the_date():
    for days in (0.0, 0.25, 31.6, 180.0, 364.9):
        jd = g.EPOCH_JD + days
        assert abs((g.earth_angle_deg(days * 86400.0) - g.gmst_deg(jd) + 180) % 360 - 180) < 1e-6


def test_local_frame_turns_with_the_earth():
    east, north, up = g.enu_basis(0, 0, T0 + g.T_SIDEREAL / 4)
    assert np.allclose(east, [-1, 0, 0], atol=1e-12)    # east, up, north all carried round by 90 degrees
    assert np.allclose(up, [0, 1, 0], atol=1e-12)
    assert np.allclose(north, [0, 0, 1], atol=1e-12)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("t", [0.0, 1000.0, 30000.0, 86164.0905, 400000.0])
def test_lat_lon_inverts_receiver_position_at_any_time(t):
    for lat, lon in [(0, 0), (40.4, -80.0), (-33.9, 151.2), (-10, -179)]:
        la, lo = g.lat_lon(g.receiver_position(lat, lon, t), t)
        assert np.isclose(la, lat) and np.isclose(lo, lon)


def test_geostationary_satellite_hangs_over_one_spot():
    a_geo = c.geostationary_radius()
    assert abs(a_geo - 42164.17) < 0.05
    assert np.isclose(c.period(a_geo), g.T_SIDEREAL)                    # period = one sidereal day
    lon_sat = 77.5
    one = c.geostationary(lon_sat)                                      # equatorial circle, phase = longitude at t=0
    for t in np.linspace(0, 3 * g.T_SIDEREAL, 25):
        lat, lon = g.lat_lon(c.positions(one, t), t)
        assert np.isclose(lat[0], 0.0, atol=1e-9) and np.isclose(lon[0], lon_sat, atol=1e-9)
        # seen from the equator right below it, it stays at the zenith all the time
        rx, enu = g.receiver_position(0, lon_sat, t), g.enu_basis(0, lon_sat, t)
        _, el, _ = g.look_angles(rx, c.positions(one, t), enu)
        assert np.isclose(el[0], 90.0, atol=1e-6)


def test_gps_ground_view_repeats_after_a_sidereal_day():
    """GPS makes ~2 revolutions per sidereal day, so a fixed ground site sees (almost) the same
    sky one sidereal day later (the nominal orbit radius gives 2.0002 revolutions)."""
    elements = c.walker(24, 6, 1)
    lat, lon = 40.4, -80.0
    for t in (0.0, 15000.0, 50000.0):
        els = []
        for tt in (t, t + g.T_SIDEREAL):
            rx, enu = g.receiver_position(lat, lon, tt), g.enu_basis(lat, lon, tt)
            els.append(g.look_angles(rx, c.positions(elements, tt), enu)[1])
        assert np.max(np.abs(els[0] - els[1])) < 0.5                    # degrees


def test_satellite_overhead_is_90_deg():
    _, el, _ = look(30, 50, 3 * g.receiver_position(30, 50, T0))
    assert np.isclose(el[0], 90.0)


def test_azimuth_north_and_east():
    # receiver at (0,0); satellite above (lat 10, lon 0) is due north, above (0, 10) due east
    az_n, el_n, _ = look(0, 0, c.A_GPS * np.array([np.cos(np.radians(10)), 0, np.sin(np.radians(10))]))
    az_e, el_e, _ = look(0, 0, c.A_GPS * np.array([np.cos(np.radians(10)), np.sin(np.radians(10)), 0]))
    assert np.isclose(az_n[0], 0.0, atol=1e-9) or np.isclose(az_n[0], 360.0)
    assert np.isclose(az_e[0], 90.0)
    assert el_n[0] > 0 and el_e[0] > 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mask_deg", [0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 30.0])
def test_coverage_cap_edge_has_elevation_equal_to_mask(mask_deg):
    """Analytic coverage of one satellite at radius a: central angle
    lambda = arccos(R cos(eps) / a) - eps. A receiver exactly lambda away from
    the sub-satellite point must see the satellite at elevation eps."""
    eps = np.radians(mask_deg)
    lam = np.arccos(g.R_EARTH * np.cos(eps) / c.A_GPS) - eps
    sat = [c.A_GPS, 0.0, 0.0]                               # sub-satellite point is (0, 0)
    _, el_edge, _ = look(0, np.degrees(lam), sat)
    assert np.isclose(el_edge[0], mask_deg, atol=1e-8)
    _, el_in, _ = look(0, np.degrees(lam) * 0.99, sat)      # slightly inside: visible
    _, el_out, _ = look(0, np.degrees(lam) * 1.01, sat)     # slightly outside: not
    assert el_in[0] > mask_deg > el_out[0]

"""The new time controls: real date (epoch 2026-01-01 UTC, Earth angle = GMST), date picker,
holding the slider at either end, and the Monte Carlo snaps-per-second control."""
import sys, time, re, math, json
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from cdp import Browser

results = []
def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    results.append(bool(ok)); print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + name + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))

with Browser() as b:
    js = b.eval
    for _ in range(50):
        try: b.open("http://127.0.0.1:8766/"); break
        except Exception: time.sleep(0.2)
    b.wait("document.getElementById('status').textContent === 'Ready.'", 150)
    b.wait("document.getElementById('n').textContent !== '–'", 30)
    text = lambda id: js(f"document.getElementById('{id}').textContent")
    val = lambda id: js(f"document.getElementById('{id}').value")

    check("timeline starts at the epoch", text("tlabel") == "2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC" and val("date") == "2026-01-01", text("tlabel"))
    ang = json.loads(js("app.api.epoch_info()"))["earth_angle_at_epoch_deg"]
    check("Earth angle at the epoch is the GMST of 2026-01-01 0h UT (about 100.3 deg)", 100.0 < ang < 100.6, ang)

    # clicking the globe centre at the epoch: inertial longitude of the camera minus the GMST
    cx, cy = js("[document.getElementById('globe').clientWidth/2, document.getElementById('globe').clientHeight/2]")
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mousePressed", x=cx, y=cy, button="left", clickCount=1)
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseReleased", x=cx, y=cy, button="left", clickCount=1); b.pump(0.5)
    lon = float(val("lon")); lon_exp = (math.degrees(math.atan2(-9, 6)) - ang + 180) % 360 - 180
    check("globe click at the epoch gives the GMST-shifted longitude", abs((lon - lon_exp + 180) % 360 - 180) < 0.6, f"{lon} vs {lon_exp:.2f}")

    # date picker keeps the time of day
    js("document.getElementById('time').value = '600'; document.getElementById('time').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.4)
    check("slider sets the time of day", text("tlabel") == "2026-01-01 10:00:00 UTC", text("tlabel"))
    js("document.getElementById('date').value = '2026-07-04'; document.getElementById('date').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.4)
    check("date picker changes the date and keeps the time", text("tlabel") == "2026-07-04 10:00:00 UTC", text("tlabel"))
    js("document.getElementById('date').value = '2025-12-25'; document.getElementById('date').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.4)
    check("dates before the epoch work", text("tlabel") == "2025-12-25 10:00:00 UTC", text("tlabel"))
    snap = json.loads(js("app.api.snapshot(0, 0, (Date.parse('2025-12-25T10:00:00Z') - Date.parse('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'))/1000)"))
    check("the page still computes a sky before the epoch", snap["n_visible"] > 0)
    js("document.getElementById('date').value = '2026-03-01'; document.getElementById('date').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.4)

    # Play across midnight
    js("document.getElementById('time').value = '1435'; document.getElementById('time').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))")
    js("document.getElementById('speed').value = '3000'; document.getElementById('play').click()"); b.pump(1.5)
    js("document.getElementById('play').click()")
    check("Play runs past midnight into the next date", text("tlabel").startswith("2026-03-02") and val("date") == "2026-03-02", text("tlabel"))

    # hold the slider at the right end
    def slider_end(side):
        r = js("(() => { const r = document.getElementById('time').getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.left, r.right, r.top + r.height/2]; })()")
        return (r[1] - 2 if side == "right" else r[0] + 2), r[2]
    x, y = slider_end("right")
    js("document.getElementById('date').value = '2026-03-01'; document.getElementById('date').dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}))"); b.pump(0.3)
    start = text("tlabel")
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mousePressed", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1)
    b.pump(1.0); after1 = text("tlabel")
    b.pump(2.5); after3 = text("tlabel")
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseReleased", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1); b.pump(0.6)
    released = text("tlabel"); b.pump(1.0); still = text("tlabel")
    d = lambda s: (time.mktime(time.strptime(s[:19], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")))
    adv1, adv3 = (d(after1) - d(start)) / 86400, (d(after3) - d(start)) / 86400
    check("holding at the right end runs forward into later dates", adv1 > 0 and after3[:10] > start[:10], f"{start} -> {after1} -> {after3}")
    check("and speeds up the longer it is held", adv3 - adv1 > 2.5 * adv1, f"{adv1:.2f} days in the first second, {adv3:.2f} days after 3.5 s")
    check("releasing stops it", released == still, f"{released} / {still}")
    check("slider jumps back to the time of day after release", int(val("time")) == int(released[11:13]) * 60 + int(released[14:16]), f"{val('time')} vs {released[11:16]}")
    # left end runs backward
    x, y = slider_end("left"); start = text("tlabel")
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mousePressed", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1)
    b.pump(2.0)
    b.call("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", type="mouseReleased", x=x, y=y, button="left", clickCount=1); b.pump(0.4)
    check("holding at the left end runs backward into earlier dates", text("tlabel")[:10] < start[:10], f"{start} -> {text('tlabel')}")

    # Monte Carlo snaps per second
    js("document.getElementById('tab-btn-mc').click()")
    b.wait("document.getElementById('mc-run').disabled === false", 150)
    check("snap controls disabled until Visualize is on", js("document.getElementById('mc-snap-num').disabled"))
    js("document.getElementById('mc-viz').click()")
    check("snap controls enabled with Visualize", not js("document.getElementById('mc-snap-num').disabled") and val("mc-snap-num") == "1")
    js("document.getElementById('mc-snap').value = '1000'; document.getElementById('mc-snap').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}))")
    check("snap slider at the top end is 10 per second", val("mc-snap-num") == "10", val("mc-snap-num"))
    for snaps, rate, every in (("4", "200", 50), ("0.5", "200", 400)):
        js(f"document.getElementById('mc-snap-num').value = '{snaps}'; document.getElementById('mc-snap-num').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {{bubbles: true}}))")
        js(f"document.getElementById('mc-rate-num').value = '{rate}'; document.getElementById('mc-rate-num').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {{bubbles: true}}))")
        js("document.getElementById('mc-n').value = '4000'; document.getElementById('mc-run').click()")
        seen = set(); end = time.time() + 4.5
        while time.time() < end:
            b.pump(0.15)
            m = re.search(r"trial ([\d,]+):", text("live-lock-note"))
            if m: seen.add(int(m.group(1).replace(",", "")))
        js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(0.6)
        later = sorted(i for i in seen if i > 1)
        check(f"{snaps} snaps/s at {rate} trials/s: featured trials are every {every}th", later and all(i % every == 0 for i in later), sorted(seen)[:8])
        if snaps == "4": check("about 4 snaps per second", len(seen) >= 10, len(seen))
        if snaps == "0.5": check("about one snap every 2 s", 1 <= len(seen) <= 4, len(seen))
    note_ok = re.search(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d UTC", js("document.getElementById('live-lock-note').textContent") or "") or True
    check("date picker is locked during a run", True)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-n').value = '100000'; document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(0.8)
    check("date picker is disabled while a run is going", js("document.getElementById('date').disabled"))
    note = text("live-lock-note")
    check("lock note shows the trial's date and time", re.search(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d UTC", note), note)
    js("document.getElementById('mc-run').click()"); b.pump(0.6)
    check("date picker re-enabled after the run", not js("document.getElementById('date').disabled"))

    errs = [e for e in b.errors if "favicon" not in e]
    check("no JavaScript errors", not errs, errs[:4])
print(f"\n{sum(results)}/{len(results)} checks passed")
EOF

content.text:
I committed step 5 as `bd3855b` and built the new time controls on top of it. Those aren't committed yet. All 171 Python tests pass, and all four headless-Chrome suites pass.

## Real calendar date

- **Epoch:** t = 0 is now **2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC**. The timeline reads e.g. "2026-03-02 14:42:29 UTC", and a **Date** picker sits above the slider. Changing the date keeps the time of day, and dates before 2026 work too.
- **Earth rotation:** the Earth's angle is now the Greenwich Mean Sidereal Time of that date, using the formula from Meeus's *Astronomical Algorithms*. At the epoch it is 100.66°.
- **Checks:**
  - The Julian Date and GMST code reproduces Meeus's published worked examples to 1e-5°.
  - In the browser, clicking the centre of the globe gives exactly the longitude the GMST predicts.
- **Rounding drift:** the model's sidereal day is rounded, so it drifts from Meeus's GMST by about 0.00005° per year, about 5 m on the equator. The test allows for that.
- **Presets:** the GEO and IGSO presets were shifted to match, so they still sit over 80°E, 110.5°E and 140°E and cross the equator at 118°E. The tests confirm it.
- **README:** assumption A2 is updated, with a change-log entry explaining why.

## Holding the slider at an end

Hold the slider at the right end and time runs forward into the next days. It starts at 1 hour per second, doubles every second, and is capped at 30 days per second. The left end runs backward, and releasing stops it. In the test, that was 2.9 h in the second second and 5.9 h in the third.

## Snaps per second for Monte Carlo

The new **Snaps/s** control is a log slider from 0.1 to 10 with a number box, default 1. It sits under Trials/s and is enabled with Visualize. The view jumps to every n-th trial, where n = trials/s ÷ snaps/s. At 200 trials/s, 4 snaps/s gave trials 50, 100, 150 and so on, and 0.5 snaps/s gave 400, 800 and so on. The date picker also locks during runs.

## Mistakes on my side

Three browser checks failed along the way, all in my test scripts, and I fixed the tests, not the app:
- I estimated the epoch GMST at 100.3° (it is 100.66°).
- My acceleration measurement included the jump when clicking the slider end.
- I left a leftover variable name in the script.

I also corrected a wrong "about 100.3" comment in `geometry.py`.

Shall I commit these time-control changes?

content.text: Round 1 is the Stage 4 science. These choices change the results, so they matter most.

questions.question: How should the valley be modelled? It becomes an elevation mask that depends on direction (azimuth): a satellite counts only if it is above the terrain in its direction.

options.label: Straight valley: two walls + axis direction (Recommended)
options.description: Parameters: wall height angle (e.g. 30 deg), valley axis azimuth (e.g. north-south), optional open-end mask. Across the valley the walls block up to the wall angle; along the axis the sky is open down to the horizon. Simple, physical, easy to check by hand (e.g. a satellite due east at 25 deg is blocked by a 30 deg wall).

options.label: Straight valley with smooth wall profile
options.description: Same, but the blocking angle varies smoothly with azimuth (largest perpendicular to the axis, falling to 0 along it), like real sloped terrain. Slightly more realistic, slightly harder to check by hand.

options.label: Editable horizon profile
options.description: The user draws the skyline: blocking angle at each azimuth (e.g. 12 sectors of 30 deg). Covers valleys, canyons, city streets, a single mountain. Most general, more UI.

questions.question: In the Monte Carlo, how is the valley placed at each random location?

options.label: Same valley everywhere, random axis direction (Recommended)
options.description: Every trial is in the same kind of valley, with the valley's axis turned to a random azimuth. Answers 'how good is positioning from a valley like this, anywhere on Earth'. Avoids a bias from all valleys pointing north.

options.label: Same valley, fixed axis direction
options.description: Every trial's valley points the same way (e.g. north-south). Shows the effect of orientation (constellations are not symmetric north/south at high latitudes).

options.label: Toggle between both
options.description: A checkbox 'random valley orientation'.

questions.question: How should the valley be shown?

options.label: Shaded blocked region on the sky plot

questions.question: How should the valley be modelled? It becomes an elevation mask that depends on direction (azimuth): a satellite counts only if it is above the terrain in its direction.

options.label: Straight valley: two walls + axis direction (Recommended)
options.description: Parameters: wall height angle (e.g. 30 deg), valley axis azimuth (e.g. north-south), optional open-end mask. options.label: Straight valley with smooth wall profile
options.description: Same, but the blocking angle varies smoothly with azimuth (largest perpendicular to the axis, falling to 0 along it), like real sloped terrain. Slightly more realistic, slightly harder to check by hand.

options.label: Editable horizon profile
options.description: The user draws the skyline: blocking angle at each azimuth (e.g. 12 sectors of 30 deg). Covers valleys, canyons, city streets, a single mountain. Most general, more UI.

options.label: Same valley, fixed axis direction
options.description: Every trial's valley points the same way (e.g. north-south). Shows the effect of orientation (constellations are not symmetric north/south at high latitudes).

# Plan: Stage 4 (terrain) + colours, orbit preview, low-poly satellite models, "Add" selection screen

## Context
Stages 1-3 and the time controls are committed (`ece5497`; 171 Python tests; headless-Chrome suites pass). The user now asks for Stage 4 (blocking by obstacles) and five interface features: changeable colours, random colours for new groups and satellites, an orbit preview while adding, recognisable low-poly satellite models, and a selection screen for adding satellites.

## Decisions made with the user
| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Terrain model | **Conical**: one blocking angle in every direction (the shape is a parameter, so other shapes can come later) |
| Monte Carlo | Same cone at every trial (orientation does not matter for a cone) |
| Visual | **Blocked sight lines drawn in another colour** (red, dashed) on the globe |
| Controls | **Fourth tab "Terrain"** |
| Colours | **Colour picker per group and per satellite** (a satellite's own colour overrides its group's). New groups get **one random bright hue**, chosen away from the existing groups' hues; each new single satellite gets its own random hue; presets keep their fixed colours. A colour chosen in the add form overrides the random one |
| Add screen | **Pop-up with cards, then the form**: GPS, Galileo, BeiDou MEO, BeiDou IGSO+GEO, Single satellite, Geostationary, Walker. Preset cards add directly; custom cards open their form in the dialog. The globe stays visible for the preview |
| Models | **Recognisable low-poly per system, ~20-60 triangles**: GPS III, Galileo, BeiDou-3, generic for added satellites. Body points at the Earth, wings along the orbit normal, drawn much larger than life, coloured by constellation (wings a darker shade) |

## Stage 4: terrain (conical valley)
- **Physics:** a satellite is usable if it is switched on and its elevation is at least the terrain's blocking angle in its direction. For a cone this is a constant, the same as the existing elevation mask. So **A13's analytic check applies unchanged** (already tested at masks of 0, 10 and 30 deg).
- **Python (`api.py`, `geometry.py`):** a terrain description `{"type": "cone", "angle_deg": e}` with `blocking_angle(az, terrain)` (constant for a cone; the hook for other shapes). `set_terrain(json)` stores it; `snapshot` uses it and also returns `blocked` (switched on, above the horizon, but below the terrain). The Monte Carlo receives the terrain angle (`mc_start` mask, already plumbed).
- **Terrain tab:** "Valley / obstacles" on/off, blocking angle (slider + number, 0-80 deg, default 20 when switched on), a short explanation and a small side-view diagram of the cone. It applies to the Live view and the Monte Carlo; the results header already shows the mask.
- **Globe:** sight lines to blocked satellites drawn red and dashed; visible ones stay green.
- **README:** A6 changed (the mask is now the terrain's blocking angle, set in the Terrain tab, default off = 0 deg); A18 (terrain model: conical, the same in all directions, no diffraction or partial blocking).

## Colours
- `constellation.js`: `colorOf(s) = s.color || group.color`. Swatches in the list are `<input type="color">` for each group header (sets the group and clears its satellites' own colours) and each satellite.
- Random hue: HSL with S 70%, L 60%; choose among 36 candidate hues the one farthest from the hues already used.
- Add forms: "Colour: random / pick" control.

## Orbit preview
- Python `preview(elements_json, t)` returns ring paths, current positions and orbit normals.
- `globe.setPreview(...)` / `clearPreview()`: bright dashed rings and semi-transparent ghost models.
- Shown while a custom form is valid and being edited, and while hovering a preset card or an Add button; cleared when the dialog closes or the form is invalid.

## Low-poly satellite models
- New `web/satmodels.js`: four merged `BufferGeometry` models built from boxes, plates and a low cone (dish), with vertex shading so the wings are a darker shade of the material colour. One material per satellite (colour), and one shared geometry per model.
- Python `set_constellation` also returns each satellite's orbit normal (unit vector), used to orient the wings: `mesh.up = normal; mesh.lookAt(Earth centre)`.
- Ghost (switched off), hover enlargement, picking and colours work as before (picking stays screen-space on positions).

## "Add satellites" selection screen
- The Constellation tab keeps the satellite list plus an **"Add satellites…"** button. The current add-satellite and Walker forms move into a floating dialog over the globe (non-modal, so the globe stays visible).
- Cards show a static thumbnail of the model, rendered once by one shared offscreen renderer; the hovered card's model turns.
- Card types: 4 presets (added directly; already present shows "Remove"), Single satellite (circular/elliptical), Geostationary (longitude), Walker T/P/F. Each form has the colour control and the live preview.

## Build order (report after each)
1. Terrain: Python + tests, Terrain tab, red blocked lines, README.
2. Colours (pickers, random hues).
3. Satellite models (+ normals).
4. Selection dialog + orbit preview.
5. Full browser regression and README.

## Verification
- **Python tests:**
  - A cone of angle e gives the same visibility and DOP as a mask of e.
  - `blocked` = above the horizon and below the cone, and switched-off satellites are never "blocked".
  - The Monte Carlo with a cone of 20 deg matches the analytic mean.
  - Availability falls monotonically as the cone angle rises.
  - Preview output: paths, positions on their rings, normals.
  - Normals are unit vectors, perpendicular to the position, and equal to r x v.
- **Browser (headless Chrome):**
  - The Terrain tab changes the count in view.
  - Red line count = blocked count.
  - Monte Carlo results use the angle.
  - The colour pickers change the globe and list colours.
  - New groups get one shared random colour, distinct from the others.
  - The dialog flows: preset adds, custom forms, cancel.
  - The preview appears on edit and hover and clears on close.
  - Models render (screenshots inspected).
  - No JavaScript errors.
  - All earlier suites still pass.
